identification.summary: UNC5337 is a Mandiant (Google) uncategorized cluster described as a suspected China-nexus espionage actor that compromised Ivanti Connect Secure VPN appliances as early as January 2024, suspected of exploiting CVE-2023-46805 (authentication bypass) and CVE-2024-21887 (command injection) [S1]. It used four custom malware families: SPAWNSNAIL (passive SSH backdoor), SPAWNMOLE (tunneler), SPAWNANT (installer) and SPAWNSLOTH (log tampering utility) [S1]. In April 2024 Mandiant assessed with medium confidence that UNC5337 is UNC5221 [S1]. A later Mandiant update states that Mandiant has merged UNC5337 into UNC5221 and that the clusters were likely related [S2]. The cluster should now be treated as part of UNC5221 in Google/Mandiant reporting [S2].
identification.firstObserved: Mandiant: compromising Ivanti Connect Secure appliances as early as January 2024 [S1]. The parent UNC5221 cluster was exploiting the same CVEs from early December 2023 [S1][S2].
identification.notes: Vendor naming: UNC5337 is a Mandiant/Google Threat Intelligence uncategorized-cluster name, now merged into UNC5221 [S2]. Microsoft's name for Ivanti-related activity is not established here; a search summary reports that Microsoft uses Silk Typhoon for activity tied to UNC5221 by Google, but Google said it cannot speak to Microsoft's attribution [S4]. Keep UNC5221, APT27 and Silk Typhoon facts separate from UNC5337 facts [S4].

attribution.sponsor: Not attributed to a government in the sources gathered. Mandiant describes UNC5337 only as a suspected China-nexus espionage actor [S1].
attribution.confidence: Mandiant: UNC5337 is UNC5221 with medium confidence (April 2024) [S1]; later merged into UNC5221 [S2]. Mandiant describes UNC5221 as a suspected China-nexus espionage actor and gives no numerical confidence for the nexus [S2]. A Google Threat Intelligence Group lead said a government link between the UNC5221 cluster and APT27 is plausible but Google has no independent evidence to confirm it (as reported by The Hacker News) [S4].
attribution.basis: Mandiant incident response and malware analysis of the SPAWN family on a compromised Ivanti appliance [S1]; cluster overlap and later merge into UNC5221 [S1][S2].

objectives: Mandiant characterizes the activity as espionage [S1]. For the parent UNC5221 on the January 2025 zero-day, Mandiant expected widespread opportunistic exploitation likely aimed at credentials and web shell persistence [S2]. UNC5337-specific objectives are not stated beyond espionage.

targeting.notes: Mandiant reports victims across a range of industry verticals and geographic regions for the Ivanti Connect Secure exploitation it tracked in 2024 [S1]. It says UNC5221 has targeted a wide range of countries and verticals [S2]. No sector or region list specific to UNC5337 is published in the sources gathered, so these fields stay empty.

capabilities.summary: UNC5337 is suspected of exploiting CVE-2023-46805 and CVE-2024-21887 on Ivanti Connect Secure and deployed the SPAWN malware ecosystem [S1]. SPAWNANT is an installer that hijacks the legitimate dspkginstall process [S1] and persists across upgrades by setting LD_PRELOAD in DSUpgrade.pm [S2]. SPAWNMOLE is a tunneler that injects into the web process and hijacks the accept function, handling traffic carrying specific header values [S1]. SPAWNSNAIL (libdsmeeting.so) exposes a limited SSH server on localhost port 8300 [S1]. SPAWNSLOTH can disable logging and syslog forwarding and only blocks logging while SPAWNSNAIL is running [S1]. In 2025, SPAWN-ecosystem malware was observed alongside PHASEJAM (web shell dropper that also blocks upgrades with a fake progress bar) and DRYHOOK (Python credential harvester), and the activity recalculated file hashes and re-signed the Integrity Checker Tool manifest to evade it [S2]. Mandiant said multiple groups may be responsible for creating and deploying SPAWN, DRYHOOK and PHASEJAM (as reported by The Hacker News) [S5]. Anti-forensics included clearing dmesg, deleting log entries with sed, and temporarily disabling SELinux [S2].

campaigns.name: Ivanti Connect Secure compromises with SPAWN malware
campaigns.summary: Mandiant reports UNC5337 compromised Ivanti Connect Secure appliances as early as January 2024, using SPAWNSNAIL, SPAWNMOLE, SPAWNANT and SPAWNSLOTH. Disclosure of CVE-2023-46805 and CVE-2024-21887 occurred on 2024-01-10 [S1].

campaigns.name: Mandiant 'Cutting Edge, Part 4' publication
campaigns.summary: Mandiant publishes SPAWN family analysis and assesses with medium confidence that UNC5337 is UNC5221. UNC5221, per the same report, moved from an Ivanti foothold to a VMware vCenter server and deployed BRICKSTORM [S1].

campaigns.name: CVE-2025-0282 zero-day exploitation begins (UNC5221 and SPAWN ecosystem)
campaigns.summary: Mandiant identifies zero-day exploitation of CVE-2025-0282 beginning mid-December 2024. SPAWN malware was previously attributed to UNC5337 and the post notes Mandiant has since merged UNC5337 into UNC5221 [S2].

campaigns.name: Mandiant disclosure of CVE-2025-0282 exploitation
campaigns.summary: Mandiant publishes details of PHASEJAM, DRYHOOK and SPAWN-family use, including Integrity Checker Tool evasion. Attribution was updated to UNC5221 on 2025-01-17 [S2].

campaigns.name: CVE-2025-22457 exploitation by UNC5221 with SPAWN ecosystem
campaigns.summary: Search summaries of Mandiant's April 2025 report say UNC5221 exploited CVE-2025-22457 from mid-March 2025, delivering TRAILBLAZE and BRUSHFIRE and also using the SPAWN ecosystem. This is UNC5221 reporting; the primary post was not opened [S3][S4].

diamond.adversary: Suspected China-nexus espionage cluster UNC5337, merged into UNC5221 by Mandiant [S1][S2].
diamond.capability: SPAWNSNAIL, SPAWNMOLE, SPAWNANT, SPAWNSLOTH; exploitation of CVE-2023-46805 and CVE-2024-21887 [S1]; in 2025, PHASEJAM, DRYHOOK and Integrity Checker Tool evasion associated with the broader UNC5221 activity [S2].
diamond.infrastructure: Victim Ivanti Connect Secure appliances were used as the persistent foothold, with the SPAWNMOLE tunneler and SPAWNSNAIL SSH backdoor on localhost port 8300 [S1]. UNC5221 has operated a likely ORB network of compromised Cyberoam appliances [S2]. UNC5337-specific external C2 is not published in the sources gathered.
diamond.victim: Organizations running internet-facing Ivanti Connect Secure VPN appliances across a range of verticals and regions [S1].
diamond.socioPolitical: Espionage by a suspected China-nexus actor [S1]; no government sponsor is stated in the cited vendor reporting.
diamond.technology: Edge VPN appliances (Ivanti Connect Secure) and their integrity-checking tooling, with the appliance used for credential theft and pivoting into Active Directory and vCenter in related UNC5221 and other cluster intrusions [S1][S2].

gaps: UNC5337 has been merged into UNC5221 by Mandiant [S2]; the encyclopedia should consider whether to keep a separate record or point to UNC5221. No UNC5221 record was checked.
No government attribution or named sponsor is available for UNC5337 in the sources gathered; the APT27 link to UNC5221 is described by Google as plausible but unconfirmed [S4].
Victim identities, counts, sectors and regions specific to UNC5337 are not public in the sources gathered.

Primary Mandiant April 2025 post (CVE-2025-22457) and January 2025 Hacker News/TechTarget/BleepingComputer coverage could not be opened (fetch errors and session limit); the April 2025 facts rely on search summaries [S3][S4].
Whether SPAWN-family tooling is exclusive to one actor is unresolved; Mandiant said multiple groups may be responsible for creating and deploying SPAWN, DRYHOOK and PHASEJAM [S5].
Microsoft naming for this cluster is not established; Silk Typhoon coverage in some reporting is Microsoft's name for related activity, and Google cannot confirm it [S4].

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Internet-facing VPN gateways (Ivanti Connect Secure) are key terrain; they hold session data, cookies, API keys and certificates and bridge to Active Directory and vCenter [S1][S2]. STEP 2: The actor persists beyond upgrades and defeats the vendor Integrity Checker Tool, so a clean scan is weak evidence of a clean device [S2]. STEP 3: Template is edge-device exploitation, then SPAWN-family persistence and log suppression, then credential harvesting and lateral movement [S1][S2]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued espionage-oriented exploitation of newly disclosed edge-device flaws, including patch-diffing to N-day [S4]. MDCOA is pre-positioned access on VPN appliances at DoD-adjacent organizations used during a crisis to harvest credentials and pivot into internal networks. Candidate indicators: SSH listener on localhost port 8300, ROOTROT-style response markers on /dana-na/auth/setcookie.cgi, modified DSUpgrade.pm, a fake upgrade progress with unchanged real version, unexpected syslog forwarding gaps, and Integrity Checker output with an anomalous step count [S1][S2].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: track Ivanti and other edge-device advisories and KEV listings and feed them to the common operational picture. (2) Authorities: factory reset and credential, key and certificate rotation require system-owner action and may need coordination across network owners [S2]. (3) Mission assurance: assume VPN-reachable internal networks may be exposed; prioritize rotating accounts used by the appliance (LDAP service accounts) [S1][S2]. (4) Coordination: share indicators through DC3 and DIB partners; because clusters overlap and are renamed (UNC5337 into UNC5221), track by behavior and malware family rather than cluster name [S2].
